source.title: Automatic Gradient Descent: Deep Learning without Hyperparameters
source.authors: Jeremy Bernstein; Chris Mingard; Kevin Huang; Navid Azizan; Yisong Yue

record.tranche_reason: The paper varies fully connected network width and optimizer and reports training and test results, using a different setup from the mapped original claims.
record.gate_note: The width and batch-size figures also report other outcomes, but only results bearing on a mapped version are included. The optimizer comparison figure describes test accuracy as plotted but gives no textual comparison or values for SGD.
record.test_reason: Figure 5 directly compares Adam and SGD training and test performance after learning-rate tuning. Figure 6 jointly measures training and test performance across widths at fixed depths, relevant to V2, although its direction beyond interpolation cannot be recovered from the supplied text. The reported Adam benchmarks also bear on V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors primarily conclude that their architecture-dependent framework yields AGD, which trains all tested architectures without tuned hyperparameters and scales to ImageNet. They report better training performance with width and the selected best CIFAR-10 architecture, but do not conclude that test error keeps falling beyond interpolation. They explicitly leave generalization and regularization largely to future work.
record.recipe_differences: AGD rather than the standard gradient methods in the mapped versions; includes width and depth sweeps, benchmark comparisons, and standard data augmentation in several experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy varies across the reported width and depth combinations; batch size also changes outcomes, though its results do not test the mapped fixed-epoch claim.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 7 reports test accuracies of 55.0%, 58.0%, 60.0%, and 59.8% for batches of 32, 128, 1024, and 4096, respectively, with training plotted against iterations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: With AGD in this experiment, larger batches generally achieved higher final accuracy; the epoch-budget relationship is unspecified.

fits_no_version.finding: The best and worst selected architectures differ in both depth and width.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AGD's architecture sweep attained test accuracies ranging from 42.55% to 63.7%; these extrema do not establish the post-interpolation width trend.

record.problems: Width and depth vary together in the reported best and worst test-accuracy examples, so their separate effects cannot be determined from those comparisons. The text does not report uncertainty estimates. The optimizer figure does not provide textual SGD test-accuracy results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on the tested mapped versions were extracted. Other batch-size results do not meet V5's fixed-epoch condition.

untested.parts: No random-label fitting or random-label held-out comparison.

No MNIST or downsampled-CIFAR-10 replication, and no explicit demonstration of training to convergence. The supplied text does not identify which widths interpolate or establish the subsequent test-error trend.
No isolation of local connectivity, learned sparse connections, or initialization from a trained convolutional network; no MNIST or SVHN comparison.
No broader optimizer tuning, decoupled weight decay, Adam-to-SGD switching, or language-model comparison.
The batch-size experiment does not establish a common epoch budget or compare the specified adaptations under that budget.
No dropout intervention or joint dropout-and-weight-decay removal.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements or ranking of generalization measures.
No removal of memorized examples and retraining.

missing.what: Record the CIFAR-10 Adam architecture comparison: depth-16, width-512 fully connected network at 53.5% test accuracy and ResNet-18 at 92.9%, with their shared training conditions and architectural differences.

Extract training accuracy and test accuracy across widths within each fixed depth, identifying any widths attaining zero training error. The selected extrema cannot replace these comparisons, and the supplied text does not reveal their numerical outcomes.
Record Adam-versus-SGD held-out performance across the ResNet-18 learning-rate grid. The supplied text describes AGD relative to both baselines but does not establish their ordering.

record.verdict_notes: Withdraw the record's V2 support verdict: neither selected extremum establishes its required trend. No V4 verdict is justified without readable held-out comparisons. The supplied text contains figure labels and captions, but does not preserve the plotted curves sufficiently to infer their ordering.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or random-label test results.

Uses fully connected networks on CIFAR-10 with AGD, not one-hidden-layer ReLU networks trained with standard gradient methods on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10. The text does not state the interpolation threshold.
No controlled comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks on the same image task.

The paper plots Adam and SGD test accuracy for an eight-layer fully connected CIFAR-10 model but gives no textual result or recoverable values for that comparison. It also compares AGD with Adam, which does not establish the mapped Adam-versus-SGD claim.
Batch size is varied, but results are not reported under a fixed epoch budget or as a comparison with smaller-batch training under the mapped conditions.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-measure comparison.
No removal of memorized training examples.
